updates.name: Kathleen C. Weathers
updates.bio: Ecosystem scientist at the Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies (PhD, Rutgers). She studies how global change reshapes processes connecting air, land and water, including fog as a carrier of nutrients and pollutants, mineral dust and black carbon, and climate effects on lakes. She co-chaired GLEON for a decade and co-designed its fellowship training program.
updates.research_interests: air-land-water interactions; heterogeneous landscapes; ecological importance of fog; air pollution; mineral dust and black carbon; climate change effects on lakes, including cyanobacteria; team science training and research

updates.name: Kathryn L. Cottingham
updates.bio: Professor of Biological Sciences at Dartmouth and Editor-in-Chief of the journal Ecology. Her group works on freshwater lake ecology and how people and lakes interact, on links between land and water ecosystems, and on applying ecology to public and environmental health, typically with a heavy statistical component. She is a Fellow of AAAS and ESA.
updates.research_interests: freshwater lake ecology; human-lake interactions; terrestrial-aquatic ecosystem linkages; ecology applied to public and environmental health; aquatic, community and ecosystem ecology; quantitative biology and biostatistics

Her listed publications cover fisher ecology in the southern Sierra Nevada, nesting habitat of cavity-nesting birds and woodpeckers, long-term bird population trends in California oak woodlands, and drought effects on western pond turtles.

He studies runoff generation in mountain and agricultural watersheds and its effects on vegetation productivity, and leads a Montana Climate Office team providing drought, climate and water data services.

updates.name: Kenneth H. Dunton
updates.bio: Professor and Department Chair of Marine Science at the University of Texas at Austin. His lab examines how changing regional climate reshapes plant composition, carbon storage and benthic food webs in coastal systems from the tropics to the Arctic, using stable isotopes, and studies the light and nutrient physiology of seagrasses, kelp and marsh plants.

updates.name: Kenneth J. Davis
updates.bio: Professor of Atmospheric and Climate Science at Penn State. He studies land-atmosphere exchange through the atmospheric boundary layer, pairing turbulent flux, trace-gas and lidar measurements with ecosystem and atmospheric models to quantify carbon dioxide and methane sources and sinks. He has led campaigns including NASA ACT-America, the NACP Mid-Continent Intensive and the Indianapolis Flux Experiment.
updates.research_interests: carbon cycle science; atmospheric boundary layer meteorology and turbulence; terrestrial water cycle; lidar remote sensing; flux measurement methods; land surface-boundary layer interactions; CO2 and methane source/sink quantification
